walkthroughs.body_html:
Operations, Finance and Influences on Business — a core area of GCSE Business Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Operations, Finance and Influences on Business brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Operations, Finance and Influences on Business.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Flow production is most suitable for:
options: High volumes of identical, standardised products
One-off bespoke products
Small batches of varied goods
Products redesigned for every customer
Selling price minus variable cost per unit
Selling price minus fixed cost per unit
Total revenue minus total costs
Fixed costs divided by output

mcqs.q: Which source of finance does NOT have to be repaid?
options: Retained profit
A bank loan
An overdraft
Hire purchase

mcqs.q: A business with a negative net cash flow in a month has:
options: Cash outflows greater than cash inflows that month
Definitely made a loss for the year
Earned no revenue at all
Reached its break-even point

mcqs.q: Are profit and cash flow the same thing?
options: Quality assurance is a certificate bought from the government.
Cash flow is the money kept in the office safe.
If a business is profitable its cash flow must be healthy.
No — profit is revenue minus costs over a period, while cash flow is the timing of money in and out; credit sales create profit before any cash arrives.

mcqs.q: Does quality assurance mean a business never produces faulty goods?
options: Quality assurance is a certificate bought from the government.
No — it reduces faults by building checks into each stage, but errors can still occur; it lowers the chance and cost of defects rather than eliminating them.
Job production is only allowed for charities.
Quality assurance guarantees zero defects.

mcqs.q: Is flow production always better than job production?
options: Mass production methods are superior for every business.
Cash flow is the money kept in the office safe.
Job production is only allowed for charities.
No — flow gives low unit costs for standardised products, but job production suits bespoke, high-value goods; the best method depends on the product and its market.
